summary: MSc Data Science student at FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg who has both run infrastructure and built the workloads that run on it. At NxtGen I operated and supported VMware virtualisation infrastructure, automated recurring infrastructure tasks, set up monitoring for cloud workloads and enforced security guidelines across managed environments. On the workload side I delivered 10+ production-ready models and built computer-vision systems in PyTorch, including object detection with YOLOv11 in a peer-reviewed paper in the ICISD 2025 proceedings. That combination is the point: I know what a machine learning and computer-vision team actually needs from a platform, because I have been on the other side of it. Based in Erlangen, available 15-20 h/week around the FAU semester.

bullets: Delivered 10+ production-ready models across 8 end-to-end machine learning projects; recognised as Best Performer of the cohort.
Built a Walmart weekly-sales forecasting model with XGBoost, reaching 96.1% R² and reducing forecast error by 18%.
Tuned a Support Vector Machine by GridSearchCV hyperparameter search to 95%+ ROC-AUC, and reached 96%+ accuracy on breast-cancer diagnosis with Logistic Regression.
Segmented 200 customers into five clusters with K-Means at a silhouette score of 0.55.
Deployed a large language model application against Google Vertex AI managed endpoints and set up evaluation loops to measure and improve output quality after deployment.
Designed and iterated LLM prompts and embedding-based retrieval on Google Vertex AI.
Operated and supported VMware virtualisation infrastructure.
Automated infrastructure tasks and set up monitoring for cloud workloads.
Applied and enforced security guidelines across managed environments.
Built an American Sign Language image-recognition system as a Convolutional Neural Network in PyTorch.
Implemented the full training, validation and inference pipeline, including data augmentation to improve generalisation.

publications.description: Computer-vision system on live CCTV feeds: weapon detection with YOLOv11 and hard negative mining to suppress false positives from visually similar objects; face recognition via a ResNet-based detector, FaceNet embeddings and an SVM classifier, with real-time alerting on detection. Reported 95.79% mAP@0.5 with precision and recall both at 0.93. Led as team leader; personally optimised the object-detection model for real-time inference on standard hardware, integrated the face-recognition pipeline with privacy and ethical considerations in the design, and tuned the system to cut false alarms while holding accuracy. Awarded Best Paper at ICISD 2025.
